next_question.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Administer oral vitamin K alone and postpone any additional reversal therapy until a repeat INR is available.","B":"Administer protamine with IV vitamin K because protamine provides rapid reversal of vitamin K antagonist therapy.","C":"Hold warfarin and transfuse platelets because platelet replacement corrects the factor deficiency caused by warfarin.","D":"Administer four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate with concurrent vitamin K for urgent warfarin reversal."}}
next_question.rationale: Urgent reversal of warfarin for acute major bleeding or urgent surgery requires rapid replacement of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors with four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate; vitamin K is given concurrently for sustained reversal. Oral vitamin K alone is too slow for this emergency, protamine reverses heparin rather than warfarin, and platelets do not replace the deficient vitamin K-dependent factors.
next_question.source_detail: Current label reviewed 2026-08-14; Indications and Usage §1 and Dosage and Administration §2.1: urgent VKA reversal for acute major bleeding or urgent surgery/invasive procedure; administer vitamin K concurrently.
